pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #14
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sentence contains only singular nouns? (1 mark)
   A. The girls carry baskets.
   B. Girls carry baskets.
   C. Many girls sing.
   D. The girl carries a basket.

2. How should you find out how your mother tongue forms plurals? (1 mark)
   A. Add s to every word
   B. Guess from English
   C. Ask an elder, a parent or the teacher
   D. Ignore it

3. Which of these words is a noun? (1 mark)
   A. tasty
   B. boil
   C. slowly
   D. millet

4. Which is a clue that a noun is plural? (1 mark)
   A. A number word such as three before it
   B. A full stop
   C. A capital letter
   D. The word the

5. How can recording your reading help you? (1 mark)
   A. You can listen back and see how to improve
   B. It ends practice
   C. It deletes the story
   D. It makes you forget

6. Which is a common mistake? (1 mark)
   A. Using a comma where a full stop is needed
   B. Using a comma in a list
   C. Ending with a full stop
   D. Starting a sentence with a capital

7. What is the guessing language game with verbs? (1 mark)
   A. Pupils read a book
   B. Pupils act a verb and others guess it
   C. Pupils write verbs on the board silently
   D. Pupils sing nouns

8. In grammar, a verb is a word that (1 mark)
   A. joins two sentences
   B. names a person
   C. names a place
   D. shows an action

9. A dialogue is (1 mark)
   A. a song
   B. a conversation between two or more people
   C. a long poem
   D. a picture

10. Which order is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Eat, go, wash, wake up
   B. Go to school, wake up, wash, eat
   C. Wash, go, wake up, eat
   D. Wake up, wash, eat breakfast, go to school

11. Which sentence should come first when making tea? (1 mark)
   A. Then pour the milk.
   B. Next, drink it.
   C. First, boil the water.
   D. Finally, serve the tea.

12. Where do oral narratives come from? (1 mark)
   A. From nowhere
   B. From elders and storytellers who pass them on
   C. From only one book
   D. From machines only

13. What is a proverb? (1 mark)
   A. A type of number
   B. A short wise saying that gives advice
   C. A very long story
   D. A page of a book

14. What is a skit? (1 mark)
   A. A list
   B. A picture
   C. A long poem
   D. A short play

15. What is a conman? (1 mark)
   A. A teacher
   B. A farmer
   C. A shopkeeper
   D. A person who tricks people to get money

16. What is a service? (1 mark)
   A. A market
   B. A thing you can hold
   C. A kind of coin
   D. Work done for others

17. Which group of words is a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. The customer in the market
   B. Pays fifty
   C. Fifty shillings
   D. The customer pays fifty shillings.

18. Which word shows a result? (1 mark)
   A. but
   B. so
   C. or
   D. and

19. The ball is touching the top of the table. Which preposition fits? (1 mark)
   A. outside
   B. on
   C. under
   D. behind

20. What does a preposition show? (1 mark)
   A. The price of goods
   B. The position of one thing in relation to another
   C. The colour of a thing
   D. The sound of an animal

21. What should you do while a classmate recites? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh
   B. Leave
   C. Talk
   D. Listen and respect them

22. What should you do while another speaker is talking in a debate? (1 mark)
   A. Talk loudly
   B. Leave
   C. Laugh
   D. Listen without interrupting

23. In the sentence Oops, it is torn, what is the interjection? (1 mark)
   A. it
   B. Oops
   C. is
   D. torn

24. What does an interjection show? (1 mark)
   A. A sudden feeling
   B. A time
   C. A place
   D. A number

25. What are notes? (1 mark)
   A. Long stories
   B. Songs
   C. Pictures only
   D. Short records of important points

26. Which sentence uses an adjective? (1 mark)
   A. The heavy computer is on the table.
   B. Computers work.
   C. On the table.
   D. The computer is on.

27. What does interpret mean? (1 mark)
   A. To tear it
   B. To sell it
   C. To explain what something means
   D. To hide it

28. What does a good form have? (1 mark)
   A. Tiny words only
   B. No title
   C. Clear title, instructions and enough space
   D. No spaces

29. What should you do after filling a form? (1 mark)
   A. Check it and sign and date it
   B. Throw it away
   C. Give it to anyone
   D. Ignore it

30. Which is a good quality of a leader? (1 mark)
   A. Cruelty
   B. Rudeness
   C. Honesty
   D. Laziness

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Read: The nurse bandaged the wound gently and the blood stopped. What does wound mean? Give two clues. (3 marks)

32. Describe how a newsreader should read a weather bulletin. (4 marks)

33. Explain what an oral narrative is. (2 marks)

34. Join the sentences with when: I counted my money. The bell rang. (2 marks)

35. Write the four parts of a telephone conversation and give a short example of one. (4 marks)

36. Write a short speech of four sentences about caring for a goat. Use at least two prepositions. (5 marks)

37. List three ways of reading with expression. (3 marks)

38. Write two compound sentences about shopping using so and but. (4 marks)

39. Explain how to take part in a class handwriting gallery walk. (4 marks)

40. Put in order: shillings the pays customer fifty (3 marks)

41. List three habits of an attentive listener. (3 marks)

42. Give three uses of capital letters in English. (3 marks)

43. Write two polite phrases to interrupt. (2 marks)

44. Compose a short poem of four lines about caring for animals. Make two lines rhyme. (5 marks)

45. Give three parts of a news item. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #14 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — The girl carries a basket.
   Girl and basket each name one thing.

2. C — Ask an elder, a parent or the teacher
   Languages form plurals in different ways, so we ask people who know the language well.

3. D — millet
   Millet is a grain, so it names a thing. The others are an action, a describing word and an adverb.

4. A — A number word such as three before it
   Number words show how many there are.

5. A — You can listen back and see how to improve
   Playing back shows where to improve.

6. A — Using a comma where a full stop is needed
   A comma cannot join two complete sentences on its own.

7. B — Pupils act a verb and others guess it
   Acting helps everyone connect verbs with actions.

8. D — shows an action
   Verbs show actions.

9. B — a conversation between two or more people
   A dialogue records people speaking to each other.

10. D — Wake up, wash, eat breakfast, go to school
   This is the natural order of a morning routine.

11. C — First, boil the water.
   Boiling water is the first step.

12. B — From elders and storytellers who pass them on
   They are passed on by word of mouth.

13. B — A short wise saying that gives advice
   Proverbs teach lessons in a few words.

14. D — A short play
   A skit is a short acted scene.

15. D — A person who tricks people to get money
   A conman deceives others.

16. D — Work done for others
   Cutting hair is a service.

17. D — The customer pays fifty shillings.
   It has a subject and a predicate.

18. B — so
   So shows a result.

19. B — on
   On shows contact with the top.

20. B — The position of one thing in relation to another
   Prepositions show position such as on, under and beside.

21. D — Listen and respect them
   Good listeners respect performers.

22. D — Listen without interrupting
   Good debaters listen.

23. B — Oops
   Oops shows a small mistake.

24. A — A sudden feeling
   Interjections show emotions.

25. D — Short records of important points
   Notes are brief points.

26. A — The heavy computer is on the table.
   Heavy describes the computer.

27. C — To explain what something means
   To interpret is to explain meaning.

28. C — Clear title, instructions and enough space
   Clarity makes forms easy to fill.

29. A — Check it and sign and date it
   Checking prevents mistakes.

30. C — Honesty
   Good leaders are honest and fair.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: A wound is an injury. Clues are the nurse, bandaged and blood.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and two marks for clues, awarding one for each up to two.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Speak clearly, keep a steady pace, use a friendly and confident tone, pause at full stops and look at the audience.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct points.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: An oral narrative is a story told aloud, passed on from person to person, that entertains and teaches.
   Working / marking points: One mark for told aloud and one mark for entertain or teach.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: When I counted my money, the bell rang.
   Working / marking points: One mark for using when and one mark for the comma.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Greet; say who you are and why you called; talk and listen; say goodbye. Example: Good afternoon, this is Neema speaking.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part and one mark for an example, with 4 marks maximum.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four clear sentences with two prepositions, for example Give the goat water beside the food. Build a shed behind the house. Do not put a heavy load on it. Call the veterinary doctor if it is sick.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence and one mark for correct prepositions.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Change loudness, change speed, pause at punctuation, use different voices for characters, use face and hands.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each way.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: I had money, so I bought bread. I wanted a toy, but it was too costly.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence and one for each correct comma.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Write your best sentence on a strip. Display it on the wall. Walk quietly, look at each strip, and leave a kind and helpful comment.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: The customer pays fifty shillings.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the words in order, one for the capital and one for the full stop.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Face the speaker, stay quiet, think about the words, wait for your turn, respond correctly (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each habit, up to three.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: The first word of a sentence, names of people and places, the word I, days and months (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each use.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Excuse me, may I say something? Sorry to interrupt, but could you repeat that?
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four-line poem on the theme with a pair of rhyming lines, for example Feed the hen at break of day, Give her water, let her play, Kind hands keep her safe and well, That is how we care, we tell.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for theme, two marks for four lines and one mark for a rhyming pair.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Headline, lead, details, quote (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.
